Subject: Question on floor bands for mixed workload

Hey Mina —

Quick clarifying question as we review the SOW: our integration will mix two main payloads — long-document embeddings (avg 6k tokens per request, ~10 requests/min at peak) and short interactive chat calls (avg 60 tokens). The proposal references a "floor per-minute band" for billing and a 1k-token minimum per request for long calls. Can you confirm how those two interact?

Specifically:
- If one request is 6k tokens do we get billed as 6k or rounded to nearest 1k band?
- If a short chat call happens in the same minute as a long embedding call, does Redwood aggregate for the floor/band calculation or do they remain separate SKU lines?
- Any examples you can attach showing an invoice line for a mixed-minute burst would be super helpful.

We referenced section 3.2 of ACME SOW v3 but the numbering doesn't map cleanly to the pricing table. If easier, feel free to send a bullet example.

Thanks — Samir

Samir — thanks for the clear questions. I'm attaching two artifacts: a short CSV that maps a few mixed-minute examples (billing_examples_101.csv) and our pricing floor table (redwood_pricing_floor_table.xlsx). See quick answers below, then some illustrative examples.

Short answers:
- We bill actual token usage rounded up to the billing quantum defined per SKU. For the long-document embedding SKU the quantum is 1k tokens, so a 6,120-token call would be billed as 7 * 1k = 7k tokens for that SKU.
- Band/floor calculations (the per-minute floor) are applied at the invoice line level after we map each request to its SKU. We do not merge tokens across different SKUs (e.g., embedding vs chat) when applying per-SKU bands. That means short chat tokens do not reduce the embedding SKU's band rounding, but they will be eligible against the chat SKU's own billing quantum/floor.
- We do offer a blended invoice line at the customer's request (single-line summary with blended unit price) but the default is per-SKU granularity which is what the SOW refers to.

Illustrative minute (attached CSV has more):
- Minute A: one embedding call, 6,120 tokens -> embedding SKU quantum 1k -> billed 7k tokens.
- Minute A concurrently: three chat calls at 45/70/60 tokens -> chat SKU quantum 100 tokens -> billed 3 * 100 = 300 tokens.
- The per-minute floor for embedding SKU is 5k tokens; because billed amount (7k) >= floor no adjustment. If embedding billed were below 5k we would top up to floor for that SKU for the minute.

Next steps: I cc'd Vanessa for pricing/discount detail and Karthik for contract mapping — if you want a blended-line payout for invoicing we can propose a blended rate and show a mock invoice.

Attaching: ACME_SOW_v3.pdf, billing_examples_101.csv, redwood_pricing_floor_table.xlsx

Hi Samir — adding the pricing nuance and a proposal for two options so procurement can pick.

Option A — Default, per-SKU bands (what Mina described):
- Pros: most transparent mapping to runtime cost, consistent with our metering.
- Cons: invoice has multiple lines; there is per-SKU rounding which can inflate small-volume SKUs.

Option B — Blended invoice (single-line summary):
- We compute total tokens after SKU mapping but present a blended unit price for the invoice line. Technically we still meter at SKU level (for routing/telemetry) and apply bands, then blend for billing presentation.
- Pros: simpler invoice for your AP team; easier to reconcile against a single PO line.
- Cons: loses SKU-level visibility and makes it harder to apply SKU-specific discounts.

Discount/packaging note: for ACME we can attach the committed-band discount to either (1) embedding SKU only, (2) chat SKU only, or (3) to the blended line if you choose option B. If you attach to blended we will calculate the effective blended discount and bake it into the single unit price.

One additional practical item on rounding/minimums: we do per-request rounding up to the quantum, but we also run a "minute-level reconciliation" where if the sum of quantum-rounded tokens for a SKU in a minute exceeds the billed floor by that SKU, we keep the higher (i.e., no downward smoothing). In plain terms: rounding never reduces your billed floor amount.

If you want, Kimberly can run the sample invoice with your expected traffic distribution and return a one-page mock invoice. Kimberly — can you take the attached CSV and produce a one-page mock invoice with both options? Deliver by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
